refutations.argument: C5 is limited to 'multiplayer Commander matches' and says the player who lost first is 'the loser of the previous game' and chooses. 903.2 says the default multiplayer setup is Free-for-All, which means other setups (Team vs. Team, 808) are allowed in multiplayer Commander. In a team game 104.2c makes every player on the winning team a winner even if that player had previously lost that game. So the first player to lose can be a member of the winning team, who by 104.2c won the game. Under C5 that winner would be 'the loser of the previous game' and would choose, which contradicts 103.1: the chooser is the loser of the previous game, and a player who won is not a loser. The stipulation is overbroad: it covers games where 'who lost first' and 'who lost the game' come apart, and it has no carve-out for team games, so it contradicts the rule it supplements. A correct stipulation would have to choose among players who lost the game (not a winning-team member who lost early), and C5 does not.

source.excerpt: The default multiplayer setup is the Free-for-All variant

steps.conclusion: A multiplayer Commander game is not confined to Free-for-All: the Free-for-All variant is only the default, so a Team vs. Team multiplayer Commander game falls within C5's 'multiplayer Commander matches'.

source.excerpt: Team vs. Team games are played with two or more teams.

steps.conclusion: A team multiplayer game with several players per team exists, so C5 applies to it.

source.excerpt: Each player on the winning team wins the game, even if one or more of those players had previously lost that game.

steps.conclusion: In such a game the first player to lose can be on the winning team and so is a winner of the game, not a loser.

source.excerpt: the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn

steps.conclusion: 103.1 gives the choice to a loser of the previous game, but C5 gives it to 'the player who lost first' even when that player is a winner under 104.2c, so C5 contradicts 103.1 on these facts.
